issues.title: Missing router import causes undefined variable error in BookerWebWrapper
issues.description: The `useRouter` hook is removed from the imports but the `router` variable is still used in multiple places within the component (lines 193, 228, 233, 239). This will cause a ReferenceError at runtime when any of these code paths are executed, such as when toggling the overlay calendar, navigating for instant meetings, or handling calendar interactions. The router is critical for navigation functionality in the booking flow.

issues.title: Incorrect priority sorting in sortHosts breaks round-robin host assignment
issues.description: The priority comparison logic is inverted when weights are equal in round-robin mode. The code now returns `priorityA - priorityB` instead of `priorityB - priorityA`, which sorts hosts in ascending priority order (lowest priority first) instead of descending (highest priority first). This causes lower-priority hosts to be selected before higher-priority hosts when weights are equal, breaking the intended assignment logic throughout the application wherever host assignment is used.

issues.title: Missing module resolution in dynamic import causes team assignment tab to fail
issues.description: The EventTeamAssignmentTab dynamic import is missing the `.then((mod) => mod)` module resolution that all other tab imports use. This inconsistency will cause the dynamic import to not properly extract the default export, resulting in the team assignment tab failing to render correctly. When users navigate to the team assignment tab for event types, they will encounter a blank screen or rendering error because the component cannot be properly loaded.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26629 - refactor: move WebWrapper files from packages/platform to apps/web/modules

structured_output.summary:
This PR relocates the web-only wrapper components (EventTypeWebWrapper and its tab wrappers, BookerWebWrapper, ConferencingAppsViewWebWrapper, SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper, AddMembersWithSwitchWebWrapper, DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper) from packages/platform/atoms into apps/web, so they can import sibling files instead of going through @calcom/web from inside the atoms package. It also moves sortHosts into @calcom/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils, exposes three event-type hooks through @calcom/atoms, and drops the WebWrapper and booker exports from atoms' package.json. The direction is right and most import rewrites check out: the relative targets resolve and the tab wrappers point at real files.

I found three real problems. BookerWebWrapper.tsx deletes `const router = useRouter()` and its import, but four `router.push` calls remain, so this will not type-check and will throw a ReferenceError on click. The sortHosts move also silently flips the equal-weight tiebreak from priorityB - priorityA to priorityA - priorityB, which changes host ordering in round-robin assignment, and no test covers it. Finally, package.json still exports ./booker pointing at a deleted index.ts. The PR's own test instruction (yarn type-check:ci) would catch the first and third, but the sort regression would only show up in production ordering.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The removed `router` binding in BookerWebWrapper is a build-breaking reference error on the booker path used by public booking pages, so it must be fixed before merge. The sortHosts comparator flip changes scheduling order for weighted round-robin hosts with equal weight and is an unannounced behavior change. The dangling ./booker export contradicts the checklist item that asks reviewers to confirm the deleted export has no consumers.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, apps/web pages and views (event-types, booker-backed public pages, team and org pages, the conferencing and calendar settings screens) rendered wrapper components that lived under packages/platform/atoms. Those wrappers imported their real UI from apps/web/modules through the @calcom/web alias, which made the atoms package depend on the web app. Platform consumers used the same atoms package, so the wrappers were exported from its package.json.

This PR inverts that dependency for the web-only wrappers. They move into apps/web/modules and import their UI through sibling relative paths. The remaining direction is web to atoms: the three event-type hooks (useEventTypeForm, useHandleRouteChange, useTabsNavigations) and SelectedCalendarsSettings are now reached from apps/web through new atoms subpath exports. sortHosts moves out of a web component into packages/lib so both apps/web and atoms can use it without a cycle.
steps: Entry points are the Next.js pages under apps/web/app and the view modules under apps/web/modules (event-types, booker-backed team and user pages, settings apps). They previously imported wrappers via @calcom/atoms/... subpaths.

The wrapper files move into apps/web/modules/{event-types,bookings,apps,calendars}/components and apps/web/components/apps. Their imports change from @calcom/web/... to same-package relative paths, and the atoms package.json drops the corresponding subpath exports.

EventTypeWebWrapper now loads its tabs via dynamic imports of ./tabs/*, so the tab wrappers and their UI live beside it. It still pulls useEventTypeForm and friends from @calcom/atoms, which are the only remaining package-level dependencies from web into atoms.

sortHosts is centralized in packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts and imported by HostEditDialogs, EventTeamAssignmentTab, and the atoms useEventTypeForm hook. Its equal-weight branch is where the regression sits.
BookerWebWrapper is the most-used moved component: public booking pages and embeds route through it, so its missing router binding is the highest-impact failure in this change.

findings.title: BookerWebWrapper uses `router` after it was removed
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookerWebWrapper.tsx`, the `router` binding was removed (along with `useRouter` from `next/navigation` and `useRef` from react), but `router.push` is still called around lines 193, 228, 232 and 238. Restore `const router = useRouter();` and the `useRouter` import from `next/navigation` (matching the original file in `packages/platform/atoms/booker/BookerWebWrapper.tsx` at the base commit). Keep `useRef` removed only if nothing else in the file uses it. Then run `yarn type-check:ci` to confirm.

findings.title: sortHosts equal-weight tiebreak order was flipped during the move
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/lib/bookings/hostGroupUtils.ts`, the `sortHosts` function (around lines 41-59) was moved from `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/HostEditDialogs.tsx` but its equal-weight branch now returns `priorityA - priorityB`. Restore the original `priorityB - priorityA` in that branch so it matches the base commit's `HostEditDialogs.tsx` version and the non-weighted branch. Add a unit test in `packages/lib` that asserts the ordering for equal-weight hosts with differing priorities, so this cannot silently regress again.

findings.title: package.json still exports the deleted ./booker entry
findings.body:
`packages/platform/atoms/booker/index.ts` is deleted in this PR, but `packages/platform/atoms/package.json` still maps `"./booker": "./booker/index.ts"`. Any consumer that imports `@calcom/atoms/booker` will fail at module resolution. This is exactly the open question in the PR's human review checklist. Nothing in the repo imports that path at head, so the safe fix is to remove the export, not keep a dead entry.

::diff{file="packages/platform/atoms/package.json" lines="57-59"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/platform/atoms/package.json`, remove the `"./booker": "./booker/index.ts"` entry from the `exports` map. The file `packages/platform/atoms/booker/index.ts` was deleted in this PR, so the export now points at nothing. Confirm with a repo-wide grep for `@calcom/atoms/booker` that no consumers remain (the grep at head found none), then run `yarn type-check:ci`.

findings.title: DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper still uses deep relative imports into packages/platform
findings.body:
The PR's "Updates since last revision" says deep relative imports were fixed to use the `@calcom/atoms` alias, but this file was only partially fixed. It now reaches four directories up into `packages/platform/atoms/src/...` and `packages/platform/atoms/destination-calendar/...`. That couples apps/web to the folder layout of the atoms package and defeats the purpose of the move, which was to remove cross-package reach-throughs.

::diff{file="apps/web/components/apps/DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper.tsx" lines="3-4"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/components/apps/DestinationCalendarSettingsWebWrapper.tsx`, replace the two `../../../../packages/platform/atoms/...` relative imports with `@calcom/atoms` package-alias imports. Add `./destination-calendar/DestinationCalendar` and `./src/components/atoms-wrapper` as exports in `packages/platform/atoms/package.json` (following the pattern used for `selected-calendars/SelectedCalendarsSettings`) and import from there. Match the style used by the other moved wrappers.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace churn in EventTypeWebWrapper tabMap
findings.body:
The `tabMap` entries for setup and availability were re-indented from the file's 6-space style to 8-space indentation, and the three renamed wrappers gained `No newline at end of file` changes. None of this changes behavior, but it inflates the diff of a rename-heavy PR and makes the actual import rewrites harder to review. Consider reverting these whitespace-only hunks so the move stays reviewable.

::diff{file="apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx" lines="236-250"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx`, revert the whitespace-only re-indentation of the `setup` and `availability` entries in `tabMap` (around lines 236-250) back to the original indentation. Also restore the trailing newline in the `EventLimitsTabWebWrapper.tsx`, `EventRecurringWebWrapper.tsx` files under `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/`. Keep the change otherwise to import-path rewrites only.

findings.title: Moved wrappers and hook exports resolve correctly
findings.body: I checked the relocated import targets against the head tree. The tab wrappers' dynamic imports (`./tabs/setup/...`, `./tabs/availability/...`, and the rest) all point at files that exist. `AppList`, `DisconnectIntegrationModal`, `ManagedEventDialog`, and `SelectedCalendarsSettings` also resolve, and the three new hook subpaths in `packages/platform/atoms/package.json` map to real files. Moving `sortHosts` out of a React component file also removes a dependency that the atoms hook had on a web component, which is a good direction for the package boundary.
